paragraphs: (1) Avot chapter 4. Mishnah: Terumot 10:9; Shabbat 20:2, 24:5; Pesahim 7:2; Sukkah 2:5; Nedarim 9:1; Eduyot 3:8, 7:1–4; Bekhorot 1:6 [Heilprin cites 1:7]; Kelim 12:4–5; Mikva'ot 5:5.

(2) R' Elazar's father. It is uncertain whether he was a priest. Although Avot De-Rabbi Natan, chapter 16, says that R' Tzadok was taken captive to Rome, and they gave him a slave-woman to lie with, and he said, ‘I am of the priesthood’—so too in Menorat Ha-Ma'or, Laws and Repentance (this is not R' Yitzhak Aboab's Menorat Ha-Ma'or)—perhaps he offered this excuse to put off the matron. In Tosafot, Sukkah 26, beginning of b, 27a; Yoma 79a–b; Yevamot 15, beginning of b; Hullin 107, end of a: he was a priest, as is evident in Mi She-Meto, 19b, and Pesulei Ha-Mukdashin, folio 36.

(3) In the Mishnah, beginning of Keitzad Tzolin, R' Tzadok said: ‘An incident involving Rabban Gamliel, who told his slave Tavi.’ In the Mishnah, Ha-Yashen, 26b: Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai, Rabban Gamliel, and R' Tzadok. In the Mishnah, end of Mi She-Hehshikh: an incident in the days of R' Tzadok's father and the days of Abba Shaul ben Botnit. In Kiddushin 32b:4–6, he was with R' Eliezer and R' Yehoshua at the wedding of Rabban Gamliel's son. R’ Tzadok said, “Rabban Gamliel, the great man, is standing and serving us drinks” [Heilprin’s excerpt]. R' Tzadok had a firstborn animal, etc.; he came before R' Yehoshua, etc.; he came before Rabban Gamliel, etc.; also R' Hutzpit the interpreter: Bekhorot 36. In Nazir 44a: an incident in which R' Yitzhak's father died in Ginzak. They informed him after three years, and he asked R' Yehoshua ben Elisha and four elders. They told him, ‘For his father’ when he is whole, but not when he is incomplete. Orah Mishor writes: ‘I found written that it should read “R' Tzadok's father,” etc., and he asked Elisha ben Avuya and the elders with him; so is the reading in Mo'ed Katan 20, end of a. R' Tzadok was a priest. But Responsa Rashba, section 294, has a different reading.’ End quotation. R' Tzadok was among Beit Shammai's pupils, and all his actions he performed according to Beit Hillel: Yevamot 15b.

(4) R' Tzadok fasted for forty years so that the Temple would not be destroyed: Gittin 56a:13. Yuhasin writes [in the chronological section] that forty years before the destruction the Sanctuary doors opened, until Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai rebuked them, as found in Yoma and Sanhedrin; he therefore knew that it would be destroyed. In Avodah Zarah: forty years before the destruction the Sanhedrin went into exile. In Midrash Eikhah, on ‘Her adversaries have become the head,’ Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai asked Vespasian to have his physician heal R’ Tzadok. His son R' Elazar told him to pay the physicians so that they would not receive their reward in the World to Come, and he taught them the art of finger calculation; see Yefeh Anaf there. In Tosefta Kilayim he said, ‘On this clean place sat Haggai the prophet.’ Accordingly, R' Tzadok would have been four hundred years old at the destruction; R' Duran likewise writes this in his commentary on the Chapters. With R' Dosa ben Harkinas. In Eikhah Rabbah, on ‘For these things I weep’: the son and daughter taken captive, who recognized one another and died, were the children of R' Tzadok the priest, not of R' Yishmael ben Elisha; see there. Perhaps this is not R' Tzadok, R' Elazar's father [Yuhasin, chronological section]. In Kiddushin 40a: ‘Mighty in strength, who do His word’—such as R' Tzadok, whom a matron solicited. He told her, ‘My heart is weak, and I cannot. Is there anything to eat?’ She said, ‘There is something unclean.’ He said, ‘What difference does it make? One who does that eats this.’ She heated the oven, and he climbed up and sat inside it. She asked, ‘What is this?’ He answered, ‘One who does that falls into this.’ She said, ‘Had I known it was so grave, I would not have distressed you.’ (See above, R' Hanina bar Pappi: it is uncertain whether this R' Tzadok whom the matron solicited was R' Elazar's father. See there also that R' Tzadok is Ephraim son of Yosef.)
